questions.q: A, Z, BY, ___
questions.e: Pairs: A-Z, B-Y, C-X. Letters from the front go up, letters from the back go down.
Add 5 each time: B, G, L, Q, V.
Add 3 each time: C, F, I, L.
Subtract 4, 3, 2, then 1: O, K, H, F, E.
Subtract 3 each time: S, P, M, J.
Go backwards through the alphabet: X, W, V, U, T, S.
Add 3 each time: B, E, H, K, N.

questions.q: A, X, B, W, C, V, D, ___
questions.e: Two series mixed: A, B, C, D and X, W, V, U. The next is U.

questions.q: A, K, B, C, L, D, E, ___
questions.e: Groups of three: A K B, C L D, E M F. The next letter is M.

questions.q: AC/B, DF/E, GI/H, ___
questions.e: Each group moves 3 letters on: AC/B, DF/E, GI/H, JL/K.

questions.q: BC/C, ___, DE/E, EF/F
questions.e: Each group moves one letter on: BC/C, CD/D, DE/E, EF/F.

questions.q: AB/B, ___, EF/F, GH/H
questions.e: Each group moves two letters on: AB/B, CD/D, EF/F, GH/H.

questions.q: AB/Y, ___, CD/W, DE/V, EF/U
questions.e: The first part goes up one letter, the second part goes back one: AB/Y, BC/X, CD/W, DE/V, EF/U.

questions.q: In the following series, what comes next? A, C, E, G, ___
questions.e: Skip one letter each time: A, C, E, G, I.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 4, 9, 14, 19, 24, ___
questions.e: Each term is 5 more than the previous one, so the next term is 29. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ___
questions.e: These are the squares of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, so the next is 6 squared = 36. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 3, 6, 12, 24, ___
questions.e: Each term is double the previous one, so 24 x 2 = 48. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, ___
questions.e: The differences are 1, 2, 3, 4, so the next difference is 5 and the next term is 12 + 5 = 17. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 2, 20, 4, 18, 6, 16, ___
questions.e: Two series are mixed: 2, 4, 6, 8 (add 2) in the odd places and 20, 18, 16 (subtract 2) in the even places. The next place is an odd one, so the term is 8. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ___
questions.e: Each term is a square plus 1 (1+1, 4+1, 9+1, 16+1, 25+1), so the next is 36 + 1 = 37. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 1, 8, 27, 64, ___
questions.e: These are the cubes of 1, 2, 3, 4, so the next is 5 cubed = 125. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Find the missing number: 5, 10, ___, 40, 80
questions.e: Each term is double the previous one: 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, so the missing number is 20. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 100, 91, 82, 73, ___
questions.e: Each term is 9 less than the previous one, so the next term is 73 - 9 = 64. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 2, 6, 18, 54, ___
questions.e: Each term is 3 times the previous one, so 54 x 3 = 162. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 3, 6, 9, 18, 21, 42, ___
questions.e: The pattern alternates between multiplying by 2 and adding 3 (3 x 2 = 6, 6 + 3 = 9, 9 x 2 = 18, 18 + 3 = 21, 21 x 2 = 42), so the next step is 42 + 3 = 45. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ___
questions.e: These are consecutive prime numbers, and the next prime after 13 is 17. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: If CAT is coded as DBU, how is DOG coded?
questions.e: Each letter is moved one place forward in the alphabet: D to E, O to P, G to H, so DOG becomes EPH. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: If BOOK is coded as DQQM, how is PEN coded?
questions.e: Each letter is moved two places forward: P to R, E to G, N to P, so PEN becomes RGP. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: If MAP is coded as LZO, how is SUN coded?
questions.e: Each letter is moved one place backward: S to R, U to T, N to M, so SUN becomes RTM. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: In a code, A is written as Z, B as Y, C as X and so on (the alphabet reversed). How is DOG written in this code?
questions.e: Each letter is replaced by its mirror letter from the other end of the alphabet: D to W, O to L, G to T. So DOG becomes WLT. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: If TABLE is written as ELBAT, how is CHAIR written in the same code?
questions.e: The letters of the word are written in reverse order, so CHAIR becomes RIAHC. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: In a code language, 'red' means 'blue', 'blue' means 'green' and 'green' means 'white'. What is grass called in this code?
questions.e: Grass is green, and 'green' means 'white' in this code, so grass is called white. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: If COLD is coded as 3-15-12-4, which word is coded as 8-15-20?
questions.e: The code gives each letter's place in the alphabet: 8 = H, 15 = O, 20 = T, so the word is HOT. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: In a code, A = 2, B = 4, C = 6 and so on (each letter's place number is doubled). How is BAD coded?
questions.e: B is 2nd so 2 x 2 = 4, A is 1st so 2 x 1 = 2, D is 4th so 2 x 4 = 8. BAD is coded 4-2-8. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: In a certain code, BAT = 23 and CAT = 24. Using the same rule, what is the code for DOG?
questions.e: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: B+A+T = 2+1+20 = 23 and C+A+T = 3+1+20 = 24. So DOG = 4 + 15 + 7 = 26. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: If PEN is coded as QDO, how is BAG coded?
questions.e: The first and third letters move one place forward and the middle letter moves one place backward: B to C, A to Z, G to H. BAG becomes CZH. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: P is Q's sister and Q is R's father. How is P related to R?
questions.e: P is the sister of R's father, so P is R's aunt. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: A is the brother of B. B is the sister of C. C is the father of D. How is A related to D?
questions.e: A and C are siblings, and C is D's father, so A is D's uncle. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Pointing to a girl, Kamran said, "She is the daughter of my father's only son." How is the girl related to Kamran?
questions.e: Kamran's father's only son is Kamran himself, so the girl is Kamran's daughter. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: X is the mother of Y and Y is the father of Z. How is X related to Z?
questions.e: X is the mother of Z's father, so X is Z's grandmother. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Pointing to a man, Sara said, "He is the son of my mother's brother." How is the man related to Sara?
questions.e: Sara's mother's brother is her uncle, and his son is her cousin. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Imran's mother is the only daughter of Zubair. How is Zubair related to Imran?
questions.e: Zubair is the father of Imran's mother, so he is Imran's grandfather. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Ali walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.e: He goes north 5 km, east 3 km and then south 5 km. The north and south parts cancel, so he is 3 km east of the start. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Hamza walks 10 m south, turns left and walks 10 m, then turns left again and walks 10 m. In which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.e: Facing south, a left turn means facing east, and the next left turn means facing north. He ends 10 m east of the start (the south and north parts cancel). Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Bilal walks 4 km west and then turns right and walks 3 km. How far is he from his starting point in a straight line?
questions.e: He ends 4 km west and 3 km north of the start. By Pythagoras, the distance is the square root of 16 + 9 = 5 km. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Early in the morning, Usman stands facing the rising sun. Which direction is on his left hand?
questions.e: The sun rises in the east, so he faces east. When facing east, the left hand points north. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Ali is 7th from the top and 12th from the bottom in a class. How many students are there in the class?
questions.e: Total = 7 + 12 - 1 = 18, because Ali is counted in both positions. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: In a row of 25 students, Sara is 8th from the left. What is her position from the right?
questions.e: Position from the right = 25 - 8 + 1 = 18th. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Asad is taller than Bashir, Bashir is taller than Chand, and Danish is shorter than Chand. Who is the shortest?
questions.e: The order from tallest is Asad, Bashir, Chand, Danish, so Danish is the shortest. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: In a queue, Farid is 3 places ahead of Gul. If Gul is 9th from the front, what is Farid's position from the front?
questions.e: Farid is 3 places ahead, so his position is 9 - 3 = 6th from the front. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: In a row, Ahmed is 4th from the left and Bilal is 9th from the left. How many people stand between them?
questions.e: The people standing between them are in positions 5, 6, 7 and 8, which is 9 - 4 - 1 = 4 people. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Choose the odd one out: Mango, Banana, Potato, Orange
questions.e: Mango, banana and orange are fruits, while potato is a vegetable. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Choose the odd one out: 3, 5, 9, 11
questions.e: 3, 5 and 11 are prime numbers, while 9 = 3 x 3 is not. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Choose the odd one out: 16, 36, 64, 70
questions.e: 16, 36 and 64 are perfect squares (4, 6 and 8 squared), while 70 is not. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Choose the odd one out: Sparrow, Eagle, Bat, Parrot
questions.e: Sparrow, eagle and parrot are birds, while a bat is a mammal. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Choose the odd one out: Metre, Kilogram, Centimetre, Kilometre
questions.e: Metre, centimetre and kilometre measure length, while kilogram measures mass. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Doctor is to hospital as teacher is to:
questions.e: A doctor works in a hospital, and a teacher works in a school. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Pen is to write as knife is to:
questions.e: A pen is used to write, and a knife is used to cut. Practice question written by Claude.

questions.q: Hot is to cold as day is to:

questions.q: Page is to book as petal is to:

questions.q: Second is to minute as minute is to:

questions.q: Captain is to ship as pilot is to:

questions.q: If the 28th day of a month is Sunday, which day will the 2nd day of that month be?
questions.e: The 2nd is 26 days earlier than the 28th. 26 days is 3 weeks and 5 days, so move 5 days back from Sunday: Tuesday. Past repeated question, recalled by candidates and shared by the owner.

questions.q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are boys. What percentage are boys?

questions.q: One dozen pencils cost Rs 60. What is the price of 5 pencils?

questions.q: Saleem has an average of 60 in 4 subjects. After the 5th test his average drops to 58. How many marks did he get in the 5th test?
questions.e: Total after 5 tests = 58 x 5 = 290. Total of the first 4 = 240. So the 5th mark is 290 - 240 = 50. Past repeated question, recalled by candidates and shared by the owner.

questions.q: A helicopter needs 50 gallons to fly 320 km. How many gallons does it need for 400 km?
questions.e: 50/320 gallons per km x 400 km = 62.5 gallons. Past repeated question, recalled by candidates and shared by the owner.

questions.q: Amjad and Ahmad keep 24 balls together. Amjad keeps 3 times as many as Ahmad. How many does Ahmad keep?
questions.e: Ahmad + 3 x Ahmad = 4 x Ahmad = 24, so Ahmad has 6. Past repeated question, recalled by candidates and shared by the owner.

questions.q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how long does 1 man take to write 1 page?
